title: The biggest mistake IT folks are making right now
oneliner: AI tools absorb the whole SDLC, so single-skill careers are over - learn prompt engineering plus the disciplines adjacent to yours.
says: The world is changing: developers will not only write code, testers will not only write test cases, operations engineers will not only do DevOps. AI tools will take care of the complete SDLC. To equip yourself: first learn prompt engineering - but prompting alone is not the solution; you must also know what happens in the dependent areas. A developer must know how to write test cases and test scenarios too.
explained: The claim underneath: AI collapses the cost of producing artifacts - code, tests, pipelines - so the human value moves to judgment across the whole lifecycle. The developer who understands testing catches the AI's shallow tests; the tester who understands code knows which failures matter. Depth in one area plus literacy in its neighbors is the new floor.

Prompt engineering sits at the center because it is the control surface for all of it - the way you direct the tools doing the producing. But his warning is precise: prompting without domain knowledge produces plausible output you cannot evaluate. The skill stack is prompt fluency on top of cross-disciplinary judgment, not prompt fluency instead of it. This is the same 'context curator' insight from reel #25, told from the engineer's side.
takeaway: T-shape yourself: keep your core depth, add working literacy in adjacent disciplines, and put prompt engineering on top of both.
